blocks.text: Why not just speed up a video? Sped-up video looks jerky and softer. A hyperlapse is built from sharp still photos, so it's smoother.

steps: Pick a **calm day**. Wind makes the gimbal twitch and puts jerks in the clip. Golden hour is best: the lower light makes slow shutter speeds easier.
Choose a scene with **movement**: traffic, people, animals, clouds, shadows.
Fit a **full, fresh battery**. You can trim a long clip later, but you can't add what you didn't shoot.
Fly to **50 m or more** (70–100 m is fine). Hovering low over people for 20 minutes worries them.

In the pro camera settings set **white balance to manual, 5600 K** (6000 K for warmer golden-hour colour), **ISO 100**, and a shutter of **½ s or slower** for natural motion blur. Add an ND filter to get there in daylight.
Turn on the **overexposure warning** (zebra stripes) to see blown-out areas.
Leave photos on **JPEG** unless you plan to edit every frame. RAW fills the card, slows processing and forces longer intervals, so the clip ends up shorter.

Open **Hyperlapse** and pick a mode. Set the **interval** (2–3 s; slower shutters and RAW need longer), the **duration** (the app warns if the battery won't last), the **speed** (0.2–0.3 m/s) and the direction.
Press the **shutter** button. The screen shows frames taken and the clip length so far.
Battery running low? Stop it. Everything shot so far is saved.

items: Point the drone at the subject and tilt the gimbal down if needed.
Choose Circle, then tap the point to orbit on the screen.
Set interval, duration, speed and clockwise or anticlockwise.
Press the shutter. While it flies, the +1 s button adds a second of clip each tap.
Face the drone the way it should travel and tap the padlock icon.
Optional: tap a point on the ground for the camera to keep facing.
Set interval, duration and speed. Check the map: the red dot is where it will finish.
Press the shutter. +1 s extends it, but the drone keeps flying away from you, so watch the distance.
Choose Waypoints, fly to each spot and tap **+** to save it. Change height and gimbal angle between points for a more dynamic shot.
The app tells you if the next point is badly placed or the turn is too sharp. Sharp turns cause jerks.
Two points is the simplest route, and ideal for sunsets.
Set interval and speed and press the shutter. There's no +1 s button in this mode.

after.title: Edit the frames in DaVinci Resolve

blocks.text: The drone saves the finished clip plus every still in a folder called **Hyperlapse**. Copy that folder to your computer.

items: Optional: batch-edit the stills in your photo editor first.
In Explorer or Finder select all the stills (Ctrl+A / Cmd+A) and drag them onto a Resolve timeline. Resolve turns them into one clip.
**Inspector › Stabilization:** push Smoothness to the top and press Stabilize.
**Retime and Scaling › Scaling: Fill** to turn the 4:3 frames into 16:9.
**Transform › Y position** to move the frame up or down; the crop gives you room to line up the horizon.

blocks.text: No computer? The clip the drone makes itself downloads straight to your phone.

items: Slower is smoother. Try faster speeds only for fun.
Shutter longer than about 1 s may force a 3 s interval.
Over a road or crowd, keep the height up and keep moving.

steps: Run the pre-flight checks (Manuals › DJI LITO X1). In DJI Fly set Max Altitude, Max Distance and Auto RTH Altitude for local rules. Fit a full battery.
Flight mode switch to **C (Cine)** for the smoothest movement, and gimbal to **Follow** mode (DJI Fly › Settings › Control).
Fly to **50–100 m** above a scene with movement.

Camera to **Pro** mode: manual white balance about **5600 K**, **ISO 100**, shutter **½ s or slower**, with an ND filter in daylight. On the DJI RC 2, the camera dial can be set to change EV, shutter or ISO.
Tap the **Shooting Modes** icon in the camera view and choose **Hyperlapse**. Pick the mode (Circle, Course Lock or Waypoints if your DJI Fly shows them) and set interval, duration and speed.
Press the **shutter/record** button to start. Watch the frame count and battery.
To stop early, tap stop or press the remote's **Flight Pause** button. The drone hovers and keeps what it has shot.
dji-lito-x1.note: The LITO X1 manual confirms Hyperlapse and Pro mode but doesn't list the Hyperlapse modes or the overexposure warning. Those come from the video, which was shot on a DJI Mini 4 Pro; check DJI Fly shows the same on the LITO X1.
